# Harrison

## Overview

- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v2 c1 P4](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0004), [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- **Origin:** New Brunswick  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- **Role:** Farmer  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** A crank  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>

## Appearance

Mr. Harrison is a fussy, fidgety little man who is very sensitive about his baldness, having only a small fringe of hair around his ears.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P22](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0022), [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039)_

## Personality

Mr. Harrison is crusty, outspoken, and unsociable, often blurting out disagreeable truths without minding other people's feelings. Despite his sharp tongue and crabbed demeanor, he possesses good qualities and a soft spot for Anne Shirley, whose presence makes him feel young again.

_Sources: [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039), [v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049), [v2 c9 P5](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0005), [v2 c9 P6](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0006), [v2 c9 P9](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0009), [v2 c9 P11](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0011)_

- Outspoken  <sub>[v2 c9 P9](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0009)</sub>

- Housekeeping for himself  <sub>[v2 c1 P6](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0006)</sub>

## Goals

- Avoid unwanted female interference in his household  <sub>[v2 c1 P6](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0006)</sub>

## History

In early April, Mr. J. A. Harrison bought Robert Bell's farm adjacent to the Cuthbert place in Avonlea and moved there from New Brunswick. He quickly gained a reputation as a crank due to his peculiar domestic habits, such as keeping no fixed meal times and washing all his dishes at once in a rainwater hogshead on rainy Sundays. He got into a heated altercation with Anne Shirley when her Jersey cow strayed into his oats, though he quickly felt ashamed of his temper outburst and accepted her apology after she accidentally sold the cow. Despite his initial gruffness, he developed a warm neighborly friendship with Anne, enjoying her visits, approving of her Avonlea Village Improvement Society efforts, and sharing pipe smoke on his veranda. Though he frequently clashed with Mrs. Rachel Lynde over her outspoken nature and requests for church subscriptions, he eventually settled into a peaceful routine with his wife, Emily, who allowed him to smoke inside near open windows.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P3](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0003), [v2 c1 P4](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0004), [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P6](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0006), [v2 c1 P7](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0007), [v2 c1 P8](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0008), [v2 c3 P1](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0001), [v2 c3 P8](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0008), [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039), [v2 c3 P46](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0046), [v2 c9 P0](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0000), [v2 c9 P11](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0011), [v2 c30 P2](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0002), [v2 c30 P4](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0004)_

## Background by volume

- Moved to Avonlea from New Brunswick in April after buying Robert Bell's farm  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- Has a brother who was a sailor  <sub>[v2 c3 P6](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0006)</sub>
- Acquired his parrot, Ginger, from his sailor brother  <sub>[v2 c3 P6](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0006)</sub>

## Quotes

> It was the truth and I believe in telling the truth to everybody.  <sub>[v2 c9 P5](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0005)</sub>

> You must excuse me, Anne. I’ve got a habit of being outspoken and folks mustn’t mind it.  <sub>[v2 c9 P9](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0009)</sub>

> I’m a crusty, lonesome, crabbed old chap, but there’s something about that little girl makes me feel young again . . . and it’s such a pleasant sensation I’d like to have it repeated once in a while.  <sub>[v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049)</sub>

> Changes ain’t totally pleasant but they’re excellent things.  <sub>[v2 c30 P1](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0001)</sub>
